messages.content: Return only JSON matching the schema. Review for exact boundaries, replay safety, and asynchronous throughput.

LISS has a legacy ActivityStreams service contract that synchronously spawns child provider CLIs, and a newer persistent cheapest-sufficient broker over a local Unix socket. The broker returns immediate admission receipts, settles asynchronously, journals results, replays by job ID plus payload digest, and bounds queue/concurrency/RPM/attempts. Root law permits LISS to own its service-specific ActivityStreams semantic contract but reserves reusable network ActivityPub transport to a separately hireable provider. A separate metered-inference-tollbooth owns x402 authorization verification and truthfully does not claim on-chain broadcast. Proposed smallest repair: run a service-specific ActivityStreams adapter inside the one persistent LISS broker process. It handles addressed Offer<ServiceSolicitation>, provider-authored digest-bound Offer<ExecutableServiceOffer>, Accept<ServiceContract> with actor-bound attenuated capability, and actor-bound Question<InferenceResultQuery>. Acceptance maps to broker.admit and returns immediately as Accept<InferenceSubmissionResult>; inquiry later returns the terminal record or typed not-settled refusal. Provider offers, contracts, submission responses, and ownership bindings are append-only LISS records and replay safely across restart. Raw NDJSON stays classified A2A; ActivityStreams envelopes are the semantic inter-enterprise face over the local carrier. Network federation is deferred to the missing ActivityPub provider. x402 stays outside LISS. Identify critical changes or reject this design. Never recommend another scheduler or synchronous waiting.
